author: Lee Voss
title: Car Crashes Into Garage After Woman's Medical Emergency - NewsBreak
text:
By Lee Voss ,
6 hours ago
ST. MARTIN TOWNSHIP ( WJON News ) — A woman from Morris had to be treated at the hospital after a medical emergency caused her to crash her Tesla into the back of a garage.
The Stearns County Sheriff’s Office received multiple 911 calls Tuesday evening about a crash south of Freeport in St. Martin Township.
Deputies responded to the area of County Road 12 and County Road 11 at around 5:30 p.m. Once they arrived, deputies found the car halfway through the backside of an attached garage.
St. Martin Rescue was able to safely extricate the driver, 58-year-old Julia Hoffman , and transfer her to Melrose Hospital by ambulance.
The sheriff’s office says Hoffman was westbound on County Road 12 when she veered off the road, crossed over County Road 11, entered the ditch, and into a small corn field. The vehicle came to rest at the end of the field, but suddenly started driving forward and struck the back side of the garage.
No one was inside the garage at the time of the crash.

Memorable Minnesota Sports Homecomings/Reunions Memorable Minnesota Sports Homecomings/Reunions Gallery Credit: Getty Images Getty Images Fran Tarkenton Tarkenton was the starting quarterback for the Minnesota Vikings' first six seasons from 1961-1967 before heading to the New York Giants, where he starred for five seasons. He returned to the Vikings for the 1972-1978 seasons. Getty Images Randy Moss Randy Moss exploded onto the scene with the Minnesota Vikings in 1998 and starred for the team until he was traded to the Oakland Raiders in 2005. Moss returned to the Vikings in 2010 for a less-than-memorable four game stint with the purple. Getty Images Jack Morris A St. Paul native, Jack Morris spent 14 seasons with the Detroit Tigers before signing as a free agent before the Twins' magical 1991 season. After one year with the Twins, Morris went on to play with the Blue Jays and Indians before retiring in 1994. Getty Images Paul Molitor St. Paul's Paul Molitor spent the first 15 years of his career with the Brewers before three in Toronto from 1993-1995. In 1996 he signed with the Twins, with whom he charted his 3,000th hit. Getty Images Dave Winfield St. Paul native and Minnesota Golden Gopher Dave Winfield was drafted by NBA, NFL and MLB teams. He ended up sticking with baseball and played for the Padres, Yankees and Angels before signing with the Twins in 1993 for his age 41 and 42 seasons. Getty Images Torii Hunter Torii Hunter was an outfielder for the Twins from 1997-2007 and helped lead a team that had been wallowing in mediocrity to four playoff appearances in five seasons from 2002-2006. After playing four seasons with the Angels and two with the Tigers, Hunter came back to the Twins for his age-39 season in 2015 before calling it a career. Getty Images Eddie Guardado Eddie Guardado was a fan-favorite reliever for the Twins from 1993 (when he was a starting pitcher) through his back-to-back all star seasons in 2002 and 2003. Guardado spent time with the Mariners, Reds and Rangers before coming back to the Twins in 2008. Getty Images Kevin Garnett Garnett joined the Timberwolves as a teenager in 1995 and led the franchise to unprecedented heights until he was traded to the Celtics in 2007. Garnett returned to the Wolves for the 2014-15 and 2015-16 seasons. Getty Images Ricky Rubio Rubio was drafted as a teenager out of Spain and played for the Timberwolves from 2011-2017 before heading to Utah. Rubio returned to the Wolves for the 2020-2021 season. Getty Images Mark Parrish Mark Parrish went to Bloomington Jefferson High School and played collegiately at St. Cloud State University. Parrish began his NHL career with the Florida Panthers in 1998 and spent time with the Islanders and Kings before coming home with the Minnesota Wild for the 2006-07 season. Getty Images Zach Parise Minneapolis' Zach Parise starred at the University of North Dakota before spending seven seasons with the New Jersey Devils to start his career. He and Ryan Suter signed matching long-term contracts with the Minnesota Wild on July 4th, 2012. Getty Images Matt Cullen Cullen is a Virginia, Minnesota native who played his college hockey at St. Cloud State University. He made his NHL debut with the Ducks in 1997 and saw time with the Panthers, Hurricanes, Rangers and Senators before signing with the Minnesota Wild in 2010-11. Cullen left for the Predators in 2013, but came back for a second stint with the Wild in 2017.
